artifacts.name: Heat-relief places explorer
artifacts.summary: The actual OpenStreetMap objects behind the heat-relief places, with their attributes. Zoom in to inspect them.
artifacts.description:
The true OpenStreetMap geometry of every counted feature — points, ways and areas — carrying its name and (where mapped) opening hours. It appears from a neighbourhood zoom level so you can inspect the individual objects rather than an aggregate.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: heat_resilience · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Heat-relief places heatmap
artifacts.summary: A gridded density of heat-relief places across the area — brighter means more. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area of interest, each cell shaded by how many heat-relief places fall within it. It reveals clusters and gaps that individual points can hide.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: heat_resilience · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Heat-relief places density surface
artifacts.summary: A smoothed, continuous density surface of heat-relief places (kernel-style). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A kernel-smoothed density of heat-relief places: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: heat_resilience · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Heat-relief places per resident (surface)
artifacts.summary: A continuous surface of heat-relief places per 1,000 residents — provision relative to need, without administrative boundaries. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Kernel-smoothed heat-relief places density divided by population density on the same grid, scaled to per 1,000 residents. Unlike the per-capita choropleth this owes nothing to administrative boundaries, so gradients *within* a district are visible; the trade-off is that it is a smoothed estimate rather than an exact count per area. Cells with fewer than 1 residents are left transparent, because dividing by a nearly empty cell produces a large figure that reflects the arithmetic rather than good provision. Populated cells with no feature within reach are drawn in the lowest class, not left blank — they are the worst-served places and the reason to read this map.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: heat_resilience · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest heat-relief place
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest heat-relief place from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest heat-relief place. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: heat_resilience · reachability: straight-line distance.
